q-95511.name: Question 1
q-95511.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{4x}-2\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{e}^{2x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{4x})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{e}^{2x}) \\  & =4{e}^{4x}-2(-\frac{1}{|{e}^{2x}|\sqrt{1+({e}^{2x})^{2}}})\cdot ({e}^{2x})^{′} \\  & =4{e}^{4x}+\frac{2}{{e}^{2x}\sqrt{1+{e}^{4x}}}\cdot 2{e}^{2x} \\  & =4{e}^{4x}+\frac{4}{\sqrt{1+{e}^{4x}}} \\  & =4({e}^{4x}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{e}^{4x}}}).\end{aligned}
$$

a

EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is ddx(arcsch⁡x)=−1|x|1+x2.

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get dydx=ddx(e4x−2arcsch⁡e2x)=ddx(e4x)−2ddx(arcsch⁡e2x)=4e4x−2(−1|e2x|1+(e2x)2)⋅(e2x)′=4e4x+2e2x1+e4x⋅2e2x=4e4x+41+e4x=4(e4x+11+e4x).

q-341470.name: Question 2
q-341470.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[2\operatorname{arcsch}⁡({x}^{4}+2)] \\  & =2\cdot [-\frac{1}{|{x}^{4}+2|\sqrt{1+{({x}^{4}+2)}^{2}}}]\cdot {({x}^{4}+2)}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{2}{({x}^{4}+2)\sqrt{1+({x}^{8}+4{x}^{4}+4)}}\cdot 4{x}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}+2}\frac{8{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{{x}^{8}+4{x}^{4}+5}}.\end{aligned}
$$

dydx=ddx[2arcsch⁡(x4+2)]=2⋅[−1|x4+2|1+(x4+2)2]⋅(x4+2)′=−2(x4+2)1+(x8+4x4+4)⋅4x3=−1x4+28x3x8+4x4+5.

q-341457.name: Question 3
q-341457.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[3\,\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(x-1)] \\  & =3\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(x-1)] \\  & =3\cdot [-\frac{1}{|x-1|\sqrt{1+(x-1)^{2}}}]\cdot (x-1)^{′} \\  & =-\frac{3}{|x-1|\sqrt{1+({x}^{2}-2x+1)}}\cdot 1 \\  & =-\frac{1}{|x-1|}\,\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-2x+2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is ddx(arcsch⁡x)=−1|x|1+x2.

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get dydx=ddx(−3arcsch⁡4x)=−3ddx(arcsch⁡4x)=−3⋅(−1|4x|1+(4x)2)⋅(4x)′=3⋅14|x|1+16x2⋅4=3|x|1+16x2.

q-95318.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{1+({x}^{2})^{2}}}\cdot ({x}^{2})^{′} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1+{x}^{4}}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{4x}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1+{x}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{x\sqrt{1+{x}^{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
